newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.1 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.1 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.1 percent to close at 1.0336 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency of 1.0335 to 1.0385, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new trading level for the fluctuation of the real by buying dollars at 1.0335 and selling at 1.0385 reais in a morning auction.
The previous mini-band, set Nov 28, was between 1.0325 and 1.0375 reais.
In the afternoon, Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0335 reais to drain excess dollars from the market.
Commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts have totaled a $268 million surplus since Nov 28, the last time the Central Bank bought dollars, dealers said.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.11 percent to end at 1.0392 following the drop in the mini-band.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed at 1.095, down 0.46 percent, traders said.
